title: Agent platforms tighten workflow control
summary: LangChainJS and Anthropic Claude Code release updates that tighten interrupt preservation and multi-turn session resilience.

items.name: langchainjs
items.what: Preserves LangGraph interrupts inside tool retry middleware instead of treating them as failures.
items.whyDifferent: Keeps paused tool calls resumable through checkpointers without converting them into erroneous tool states.

items.name: claude-code
items.what: Terminal coding assistant adding session resume resilience and permission stack counters.
items.whyDifferent: Prevents dropped turns after parallel tool calls and introduces structured mouse support for fullscreen list navigation.

readThrough: Agent engineering tooling is prioritizing interruption safety and state durability over simple execution speed. Teams building production LLM apps must adopt frameworks that cleanly handle paused tasks and interrupted tool histories without breaking checkpoint continuity.

social.linkedin: Agent platforms are shifting focus toward state durability and interrupt recovery. The latest releases from LangChainJS and Anthropic's Claude Code emphasize preserving tool execution state and maintaining continuity across interrupted turns. For engineering teams, this means agent architectures are maturing past simple retry loops into robust systems capable of pausing and resuming safely without corrupting checkpointer histories. Evaluation must now include how frameworks handle unexpected breaks during multi-step tool calls.
